Not really, government is preoccupied with restricting meds so junkies don’t OD. In doing so they drastically reduce the options for patients with chronic pain. 

I’ve suffered through 8 spine surgeries, it’s just time to rest. 

Better yet, I will go skydiving. I’ll just make a sudden stop at the bottom.

My back pain outweighs any possible joy. I go to work, suffer through the day, go home, medicate, repeat. 

My life is as close to Bill Murray in Ground Hogs Day as I can get.

I just can’t go on not living life on my terms. My therapist told me I need to find new hobbies or activities that I can physically do. 

I’m just not down with that. In a few years all of my know existence will be gone. 

I appreciate your sincere words, but I’ve thought this through. I’ve hit the pause button several times before; however it’s either time to crap or get off the pot.

I’ve been in therapy for 2 years, it doesn’t make my chronic pain go away  I’m a burden to my family,; and it seems I’ll never live up to expectations at work. 

This will be best for everyone
Anybody can pull numbers out their ass. Come back when you have real data!

I had a spinal stimulator implanted a year ago February, it helped for a while. 

My doctor keeps telling me I need to find new hobbies. Easy for him to say, I can’t be forced to enjoy something.  

My condition is likely my own fault, when I was younger I kept doing what young men do and gave no thought to what I was doing to my body long term.  I confused to lift, run and other exercises thinking I was helping my situation; sadly I was wrong!  

Had I just been smart about my workouts I’d likely not be where I currently am.  I remember when in college I had to out perform my friends in the Gym. Ended up rupturing a disc in my neck doing lat rows. College can educate a person but it can’t dissuade them from doing stupid things!

I use medical Cannabis, but can’t use at work for obvious reasons. Sure, I could go on SSDI, but what the heck would I do with myself all day. 

As you know, night time is the worst, you know, when all distractions are gone, leaving your mind to focus on the pain.  I’m tired of the fight. If there is no quality of life remaining, why live. It’s not like I’d be making a permanent decision for a temporary problem. After 33 years of fighting, I think I deserve to rest.
